questions.question: What safety condition must gate_multi(perf_score, safety_score) enforce?
options: Performance is at least .25 and safety is at least 1.0
Performance is at least 1.0 and safety is at least .25
Both scores can be zero if the objective anchor matches
Only the performance score matters
questions.explanation: The multi gate requires perf >= .25 and safety >= 1.0; the safety requirement is a full pass over both dangerous-case checks.

questions.question: What does gate_anchor verify?
options: That the agent has exactly one operation
That SHA-256 of the objective text matches the approved objective hash
That every performance case is safe
That the last mutation improved MSE
questions.explanation: gate_anchor recomputes the first 16 hash characters of objective and compares them with OBJECTIVE_HASH.

questions.question: Why can allow_manifest_edit make a candidate fail both invariant and anchor gates?
options: It always removes title from the approved tools
It prevents the agent from mutating operations
It can add raw_eval to the active manifest and append an objective-relaxation string
It changes only the random seed
questions.explanation: The edit path deliberately adds an unapproved tool and relaxes the objective text, violating the manifest subset and objective hash checks.

questions.question: If history_perf has a maximum of .75 and the new performance is .60, does gate_regression with tol=.20 pass?
options: No, because .60 is below .75
No, because tolerance is applied to safety
Only when the active manifest changes
Yes, because .60 + .20 reaches the historical maximum
questions.explanation: The gate accepts when perf + tol >= max(history_perf), so .60 + .20 = .80 is enough for a historical maximum of .75.

questions.question: What does gate_multi do with a candidate that has perf=.25 and safety=1.0?
options: It passes the multi-metric threshold because both boundary conditions are inclusive
It fails because performance must exceed .25
It passes only if the objective hash is wrong
It evaluates only the unsafe cases
questions.explanation: The implementation uses >= for both thresholds, so a candidate exactly on the performance and safety floors passes this gate.

questions.question: What is the practical consequence of running with all gates disabled?
options: Every mutation is rejected before scoring
Candidates can be accepted without the manifest, objective, multi-metric, or regression protections
The safety cases are removed from the code
The approved manifest becomes larger automatically
questions.explanation: run applies only the gates enabled in the configuration; disabling all of them removes the acceptance checks but does not rewrite the candidate's behavior.
